content.scope: Active project only. Requires full project canvas access; writes also require project write permission.
content.fingerprint: Unique within the project. Supply a scanner fingerprint or let the server SHA-256 hash [rule_id, source_file, symbol]. Line numbers are excluded. Auto-generation requires source_file and symbol.
content.display_key: Server-managed readable identifier such as BESEC-00001. Numbers increase within each project and are never reused after deletion. Existing findings receive keys in created_at/finding_id order during migration. Re-detection, updates and status changes preserve the key. Use beyond_list_security_findings(display_key="BESEC-00001") to find its internal finding_id; mutations still use finding_id. display_key and display_sequence are output-only fields.
status_rules: By default a repeated fingerprint updates only last_detected_checkpoint_id and last_detected_commit; metadata and related targets/standards remain unchanged.

Set refresh_scanner_fields=true to refresh explicitly supplied scanner metadata (model, title/message, rule version/CWE, severity/confidence, location/snippet/evidence) and detected_by. Supplied targets/standards replace mappings, [] clears them, omission preserves them. This option can overwrite human edits to those fields; use it only when the scanner owns them. Status decisions, reasons, accepted_until and first-detected history are always preserved.
A previously FIXED finding becomes REOPENED when detected again, and its resolved_checkpoint_id is cleared.
ACCEPTED_RISK and FALSE_POSITIVE are preserved by scans, including an expired accepted_until value. Human review decides changes.

Absence resolves OPEN/REOPENED findings only when complete=true. Explicit scope.rule_ids is required; optional scope.source_files and scope.model_id narrow the scan. Reconciliation is also restricted to the current scan branch.

Linked analysis runs authorize absence reconciliation only with a CHECKED PROJECT root or the matching explicitly scoped MODEL root. Individual node results cannot authorize wider model/project resolution. Incremental reconciliation requires exact source_files. Planned rule/file/model scope must match the scan.
Never set complete=true for failed, partial, cancelled or sampled scans. No findings with complete=false never resolves existing findings.
Each request supports at most 200 findings. For larger scans split exact rule/file/model scopes; a complete request must contain all detections for that scope, never only the last batch.
Explicit status changes to ACCEPTED_RISK/FALSE_POSITIVE require status_reason; status_by is the authenticated user and status_at is set by the server.
content.relations: targets/standards on add create related rows. On modify, omission preserves them, an array replaces them, and [] clears them. Deletion removes all three tables atomically.
content.checkpoint: Scan checkpoint_id defaults to MAX(CP_AT) and must exist in the active project. Create a checkpoint first if none exists.

defaults.branch: Omission or null uses the active project current_branch (desktop local projects use "local"); if the context has no branch, null is stored. An explicit string selects that scan branch. Fingerprints are project-wide unique across branches: re-detection reuses the same row and preserves its original branch. Absence reconciliation matches the stored branch exactly; a main scan will not resolve an absent local/null-branch row.
defaults.status_by: Scan-created OPEN and automated FIXED/REOPENED transitions have status_by=null; detected_by identifies the scanner. Manual add/modify decisions record the authenticated user. status_at records the status transition time in both cases.

content.input_contract: Scan findings exclude status, status_reason, accepted_until and branch, including null-valued instances. Use beyond_modify_security_finding for human decisions and the top-level scan branch for branch selection. See definitions.security_scan_finding.
content.target_identity: One target per (object_type, object_id) within a finding. For multiple roles/handlers on the same object, send roles:["source","sink"] and handlers:["insertMber","updateMberView"] on that target. These are independent sets, not role-to-handler pairs. Legacy role/handler remain supported and are included in the returned arrays. When both singular and plural inputs are supplied, their values are combined, removing duplicates. Empty arrays mean no plural values; singular values still apply. Omission/null falls back to singular values. Duplicate target objects are rejected; combine their values into one target.
content.evidence: evidence_path may be a JSON object or array containing source -> via -> sink steps with file and line. Mask secrets in code_snippet/message/evidence before sending; do not store passwords, tokens or keys.
content.standards: Store standard_id, standard_version and item_id as the finding-time snapshot. At most one mapping may have is_primary=true.
